channel.description: The news, verified. Independent geopolitical news.

item.title: The US-Israel war on Iran: reported US strikes hit Qeshm Island as Trump says a deal is coming together
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reported US strikes on Qeshm Island on Monday, described by US officials as limited and defensive against surface-to-air missile threats to US assets — no damage or casualty figure is verified — even as Trump said a deal was 'coming together very nicely'; Thursday brought a sharper split: Tehran warned any renewed US attack would bring 'long and painful strikes' on US regional positions, Axios reported Trump was briefed on further-strike plans, and Senator Blumenthal said an imminent strike was 'very much on the table' — while no strike decision is reported and the US proposal remains under review in Tehran. Thursday evening brought the post-midterm split into the open: Vance blamed the war for the defeat, Qalibaf mocked the post, and two Reuters sources said Trump was still likely to order renewed strikes — while no strike decision is reported. Overnight, Trump said a decision is coming — ‘You will know soon enough’ — and that US forces are ‘locked and loaded’; Reuters reported Iran has sent a nuclear proposal to Washington via Qatar, to be discussed only after the US meets Tehran’s seven demands. No strike order is reported. Trump also acknowledged on Thursday that 18 US service members have died in the conflict — his figure, not independently verified. Iraq's foreign minister warned on Thursday that the war 'has not stopped', and Fox News reported Trump met his security team to weigh resuming operations. Friday midday, Eurasia Group cut its estimated chance of renewed US strikes to 60% from 65% — but also cut the chance of a deal to 10% from 20%, raising a prolonged standoff to 30%. Friday afternoon, Iraq's prime minister told Trump in a Thursday call that Iraqi territory must not be used as a launch point for attacks on neighbours, as US envoy Tom Barrack met him in Baghdad. Friday afternoon also brought a Qatar track: Trump called Emir Sheikh Tamim, who pressed continued dialogue, avoiding escalation, freedom of navigation in Hormuz and secure energy supplies.

item.title: Saudi-led coalition launches large-scale operation against Ansar Allah as the Red Sea–Hormuz corridor tightens
item.description: Yemen's government forces say they recaptured positions in northern Lahij, a claim contested by Ansar Allah's earlier account of holding the al-Maqatirah ground — with no independent verification of who holds it — as the Red Sea–Hormuz corridor fighting continues. The Presidential Leadership Council claims about 20,000 Ansar Allah fighters were taken out of action in the offensive's first month — unverified, and at odds with the government's own earlier 16,100 figure. On Friday the coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles fired toward Najran — debris fell and damage is being assessed; the interception is the coalition's claim, not independently confirmed. Friday afternoon the coalition also said it intercepted a drone in the Makkah region — Ansar Allah denies targeting the holy city; the intercept is the coalition’s claim, not independently confirmed. Friday evening, airstrikes hit a crowded market in Taiz's al-Waziyah district, killing at least 20 people according to Ansar Allah's health ministry — but Taiz authorities deny any airstrikes took place and blame Ansar Allah; the Sanaa health ministry's cumulative toll rose to 276 killed and 654 wounded.

item.title: One year on, Gaza's promised 'day after' has not arrived — AP
item.description: A year after the US-brokered ceasefire took effect, all captives are home but Israel controls ~70% of Gaza, reconstruction has not begun, and strikes continue — medics report at least three Palestinians killed in Monday strikes in Khan Younis and Al-Mussadar, with a second agency reporting two. MSF analysis reported Thursday put hard numbers behind the malnutrition picture: in a 201-mother NICU cohort, more than half were malnourished during pregnancy, 90% of their babies were premature and 84% had low birth weight. Washington announced on Wednesday that the truce has entered Phase Two, and Netanyahu objected to the new Gaza Executive Board's composition.

item.title: Shipping and insurance markets are repricing the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Brent traded near $99 on Friday morning, still heading for a weekly fall of about 13% despite rebounding 3.9% to close Thursday at $98.29 as new tanker attacks fed supply worries; WTI closed at $90.52 — even as the UN maritime chief reiterated on Monday that no one should transit the Strait of Hormuz, saying he cannot confirm mines have been cleared, disputing the US military's clearance claim. Friday midday, Brent traded $99.52–$100.75, still on course for a weekly fall of about 12–13%, as Eurasia Group cut both strike odds (60%) and deal odds (10%). Friday evening, India's HPCL said it is struggling to book tankers to lift crude through the strait even as flows recover — vessel availability, not crude supply, is the constraint, its chairman told Bloomberg.

item.title: Putin meets Pezeshkian in Ashgabat and pledges mediation
item.description: The Russian president met his Iranian counterpart ahead of the CIS summit, offering to mediate as the war on Iran grinds into its eighth month. Tehran has since rejected the mediation proposal, Iranian officials said, holding to its seven conditions for any talks.

item.title: Trump and Putin struck a diesel deal to blunt Iran-war fuel prices
item.description: Over 300,000 metric tons of Russian fuel would flow under a temporary US sanctions lift, easing the price shock from the war on Iran — but analysts doubt it will be enough.

item.title: G7 weighs a 100-million-barrel oil release to steady war-time markets
item.description: The G7's 100-million-barrel release is now being implemented through the IEA — Germany will release up to 15 million barrels, France announced a 10-million-barrel release, and Italy says it has met its 10-million-barrel commitment.

item.title: Russia is supplying missiles to Iran as Tehran rebuilds its arsenal, report says
item.description: A Reuters investigation traces how Iran keeps rebuilding missile and drone stocks through a 5,000-agency procurement network importing at least $2 billion of military-related goods since January 2025, despite the US naval blockade — the latest evidence of Tehran rebuilding its arsenal.

item.title: US sanctions the entire ICC — Rubio vows to dismantle it 'brick by brick'
item.description: The US sanctioned the Hague court as an institution on Oct 9, hours after a former ICC judge won the Nobel Peace Prize — demanding the Netanyahu/Gallant warrants be dropped and issuing an April 2027 ultimatum. Canada, France, Germany, Japan and the UK rejected the move.

item.title: Treasury license would let Russian diesel flow through April 2027
item.description: The diesel deal's sanctions carve-out reportedly extends through April 2027 — turning a wartime fix into a year-plus arrangement.
